name: cudnn_affine_grid_generator
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::cudnn_affine_grid_generator(Tensor theta, int N, int C, int H, int W) -> Tensor grid. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract. All supplied registered signatures, verbatim: aten::cudnn_affine_grid_generator.out(Tensor theta, int N, int C, int H, int W, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); aten::cudnn_affine_grid_generator(Tensor theta, int N, int C, int H, int W) -> Tensor grid. The representative overload is not exclusive; original Gems pytest defines the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation to support. The pytest requires the out= variant (keyword-only out) to return the same tensor object passed in, to write the result into it and to mutate it, to raise RuntimeError when the out buffer dtype differs from theta's dtype, and it exercises autograd/backward. No test may be removed or adapted to fit this one signature. Semantics: theta has shape (N, 2, 3) (a strided view is a valid operand) and holds the affine parameters; the operator emits the normalized sampling grid of shape (N, H, W, 2) with theta's dtype (float16, float32 and, where the backend supports fp64, float64). On the CUDA/NVIDIA backend the pytest asserts that the cuDNN dtype table rejects bfloat16, integer, bool and float8 types; that expectation is bound to that backend and other backends' error behaviour is not asserted. C is ignored metadata, so 0, negative and large C values are all valid. N must equal theta.size(0) or RuntimeError is raised, H/W must be positive (zero or negative extents raise RuntimeError), theta must be rank-3 with trailing dims (2, 3), and unit H/W extents are valid, producing the clamped -1 coordinate.
